title: Distillation-Enhanced Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation for Satellite Communication Networks
authors: Lia Suci Waliani, Georges Kaddoum, Mahdi Chehimi, Shahan Hawatian
abstract: Quantum teleportation (QT) over satellite-based free-space optical (FSO) channels is a promising approach for long-distance quantum communication. However, its performance is significantly degraded by atmospheric loss and turbulence. In this paper, we investigate continuous-variable (CV) QT in a dual-downlink scenario, where a satellite distributes entangled states to two ground stations. To mitigate channel-induced degradation, we employ a non-Gaussian entanglement distillation protocol based on the sequential application of photon addition and photon subtraction (PA-PS) on the weaker channel. The results show that the proposed scheme improves teleportation fidelity by up to 7.7% and enhances entanglement negativity by approximately 105% in the low-to-moderate (below 600 km) loss regime. In addition, we identify an optimal squeezing parameter that balances entanglement strength and noise sensitivity. Taken together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of PA-PS distillation for improving CV quantum communication in realistic satellite networks. We further characterize the trade-off between fidelity gain and the heralded success probability of the protocol.
summary: This paper proposes using a non-Gaussian entanglement distillation technique, specifically Photon Addition–Photon Subtraction (PA-PS), to boost the performance of continuous-variable quantum teleportation over satellite links. By mitigating channel degradation caused by atmospheric loss and turbulence, the method significantly improves both fidelity and entanglement measures in realistic communication scenarios.
main_problem: Quantum teleportation over satellite-based free-space optical channels suffers significant performance degradation due to atmospheric loss and turbulence.
main_result: Employing a non-Gaussian entanglement distillation protocol (PA-PS) significantly improves teleportation fidelity by up to 7.7% and enhances entanglement negativity by about 105% in low-to-moderate loss regimes.
method: The authors model the process using continuous-variable quantum information theory, applying sequential Photon Addition–Photon Subtraction (PA-PS) distillation on the weaker channel before executing the Braunstein-Kimble teleportation protocol.
model_or_system: The system is a dual-downlink Free Space Optical (FSO) link connecting ground stations to a satellite. The resource state is modeled as a Two-Mode Squeezed Vacuum (TMSV) state, and the channel degradation incorporates diffraction loss, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence effects.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to apply PA-PS distillation selectively to the weaker of the two downlink channels, and it models complex physical losses like diffraction and turbulence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dual-downlink FSO quantum link setup and show how the CV-QT process incorporates the selection of the weaker link for PA–PS distillation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem (lossy satellite QT), then details the physical modeling of channel degradation (diffraction, turbulence), introduces the PA-PS distillation protocol applied to the weakest link, and finally calculates the resulting fidelity and entanglement improvements compared to non-distilled scenarios.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical limitations in quantum communication channels by integrating advanced quantum resource enhancement techniques (entanglement distillation) with detailed physical propagation models relevant to free-space optics.
